-----
 For the petitioner: Mr. Dilip Kumar Jaiswal, Advocate.
 For the State: Addl. P.P.
 ------
02/27.08.2018.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioner is an accused for the offence punishable under sections 429, 406, 188, 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, under section 11 (a)(d)(e)(ii)(k) of the Prevention of Cruelty to the Animals Act,
under section 3 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001 and under section 55 of the Food Safety and Standard Act.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to the Animals Act
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is alleged that 10 unclaimed camels were seized and were entrusted to this petitioner and others with a direction to produce after Bakrid, but the petitioner and others failed to produce the said camels.
Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 25.07.2018 and two co-accused persons have been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in B.A. No. 4538 of 2018.
Taking into consideration the period of custody and the nature of allegation, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner, namely, Md. Heyat Ansari is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bermo at Tenughat, in connection with Penk Narayanpur P.S. Case No. 41 of 2017, corresponding to G.R. No.
798 of 2017.
